messages.content: The Kansas City host finally answered. Monday room access is 3:00 to 5:30, they can lock up my demo materials, and Wednesday could run until 4:15. Can we book the sensible version now?

Yes. I’d put the options in this order: 1) Practical lead: Monday TPA-MCI via Atlanta, 9:35 a.m.-12:48 p.m., then Thursday MCI-TPA via Atlanta, 2:35 p.m.-8:18 p.m., $426 Main Cabin. 2) Cheapest: later Monday arrival around 2:05, only $38 less but too tight for the 3:00 setup. 3) Wednesday-night return: not worth it if class can run until 4:15. For lodging, the suite hotel is the cleaner choice; the clinic-rate hotel still cannot confirm the room setup.
The Thursday flight doesn’t feel too early? I do not want to finish Wednesday late and then be up at 5.

The 2:35 p.m. Thursday return is the safe middle. You can check out around 11, return the rental around noon, and still have airport buffer. The later 5:55 p.m. option gets you back to Tampa close to midnight, and the morning return is the one I’d avoid.
Good. Book the practical flight. And book the suite hotel if the cancellation terms are not ugly.

Hotel terms are acceptable: pay at property, free cancellation until Friday at 6:00 p.m. before arrival; after that it is one night plus tax. Rate is $154/night before taxes, parking included. Room listed as queen studio with coffee maker, mini-fridge, fitness room, and indoor pool. Caveat: no hot tub listed.
No hot tub is fine for this one. The clear room setup matters more. Use my saved card to hold it.
Done. Before I ticket the flight: Main Cabin includes seat selection now. Window seats are open on all four legs: 16A TPA-ATL, 21A ATL-MCI, 18A MCI-ATL, and 14A ATL-TPA. Do you want those?
Yes, grab the windows. What about getting around there?

Rideshares are pricing around $150-$185 total if nothing surges. A compact rental is $206 total, pay at counter, unlimited miles. Since you have clinic setup, a grocery stop, and two morning commutes, I’d take the compact rental unless you really want to avoid driving.
Book the compact, not prepaid. No giant SUV substitution if they ask.
Booked: compact car at MCI, pay at counter, confirmation MCI-C4372. I added a note requesting compact or standard sedan only, no SUV upgrade unless you approve it at pickup.
Give me the plain caveats before I close this.

Plain caveats: flight changes would follow airline credit rules, not a cash refund unless the airline makes a major schedule change. Hotel cancellation is free only until Friday 6:00 p.m. before arrival. Suite has pool and fitness room but no hot tub. Rental is pay-later, but fuel, tolls, and late return fees are on you. Monday works if the flight is close to on time; if the rental counter is slow, skip the hotel stop and go straight to the clinic.
Perfect. Put Monday in as airport, rental, hotel bag drop only if time, clinic by 3, and groceries after setup.

Set. Monday plan: land MCI 12:48, aim to be in the rental car by 1:25, hotel bag drop around 2:05, leave by 2:35, clinic by 3:00. If you are not leaving the rental lot by 1:40, skip the hotel and go straight to the clinic. Setup runs 3:00-5:30, demo materials stay in locked storage, then grocery/dinner after setup.

I’d keep it. New arrival is 1:13 p.m. Central instead of 12:48. It tightens Monday but does not break it. Rebooking to the earlier lane adds $190 and puts you back into a very early Tampa departure.
Map it out, because I don’t want Monday to turn into a sprint.

Revised Monday: land 1:13, deplane and reach rental by about 1:35, leave MCI by 1:50, hotel by 2:25, quick bag drop, leave hotel 2:35, clinic 2:50-2:55. If the rental line is not moving by 1:50, skip the hotel and drive straight to the clinic.
The clinic map says visitor parking is on the opposite side from the rehab entrance. Annoying.

Use the rehab entrance first for unloading, call the unlock contact, and drop the demo bins inside. Then move the car to the visitor lot. Build in 8-10 minutes for the walk back from the lot, especially Tuesday and Wednesday mornings.
What time should I leave the hotel Tuesday and Wednesday? Class starts at 8:30.

Leave the hotel at 7:35 both mornings. That gives you the drive, parking, the walk from the visitor lot, and a calm room reset by about 8:05. If it is raining or you need to carry extra equipment, leave at 7:25.
And Thursday still works with checkout and the afternoon flight?

Yes. Check out around 11:00, leave the hotel by 11:10, fuel near the airport, return the car around 12:05, and be inside MCI by 12:20 for the 2:35 p.m. flight. Grocery stop is now optional after Monday setup only; don’t squeeze it in before the clinic.

messages.content: New trip: Portland in late July. It is a Saturday-Sunday pediatric orthotics lab at a university facility. I need the options grouped by what is actually workable, not just the cheapest.

Got it. For Portland, the big decision is how much Friday margin you need before the early Saturday lab. Do they expect you to see the room Friday, and is Sunday likely to run late enough that Monday is the return day?
Yes to both. I want to land Friday with time to check in, review the lab layout, and not be wrecked. Sunday debrief could go to 5:30 or 6, so Monday return is cleaner.

Then I’d rank the outbound flights this way: Best practical choice: Friday 8:05 a.m. TPA-PDX via Dallas, lands 1:42 p.m., about $528 Main Cabin. Enough time for hotel check-in and campus walk-through. Acceptable but tighter: 10:40 a.m. via Denver, lands 4:18 p.m., about $466. Works only if Friday lab access is late afternoon. Cheapest: 1:55 p.m. via Atlanta, lands 8:50 p.m., about $392. I would not use that if Friday setup matters.
Don’t keep dangling the cheap one if it sets up a bad Saturday. It sounds like a false economy.

Agreed. I’ll treat the 8:05 a.m. as the lead and the 10:40 a.m. as the backup only if the host says a Friday walk-through after 5 is fine. The late arrival drops out unless Friday access becomes irrelevant.
What are the Monday return patterns? I would rather not land in Tampa after midnight if there is a reasonable alternative.

Three useful patterns: Functional return: PDX 12:15 p.m. via Dallas, arrives TPA 10:05 p.m., about $506. True afternoon departure: PDX 2:45 p.m. via Atlanta, arrives TPA 12:28 a.m., about $468, cheaper but rough for Tuesday. Early return: PDX 6:10 a.m., arrives 5:35 p.m., about $438, but it forces a very early checkout after two teaching days. I’d lead with the 12:15 p.m.
Lead with safe Friday and the 12:15 Monday for now. Now the hotel question: campus guesthouse versus the suite hotel nearby.

Shortlist by practicality: Campus guesthouse is the proximity pick: 4-6 minute walk to the lab, about $149/night, likely easiest if materials can stay on campus. But reviews are older and around 3.8-3.9, and the room details are thin. Nearby suite hotel is the reliability pick: 1.8 miles from campus, about $189/night, stronger recent reviews around 4.4, queen studio listed, coffee maker, mini-fridge, fitness room, and indoor pool. Caveat: no hot tub listed, and you would need rideshare or campus parking sorted.
The guesthouse room details are what worry me. I cannot be guessing about coffee and a fridge before a lab weekend.

That is the weak spot. The guesthouse page only mentions shared lounge coffee and does not clearly confirm an in-room refrigerator or mini-fridge. Bedding is listed as “standard room,” not clearly queen. Fitness access appears to depend on campus rec guest-pass rules, and there is no pool or hot tub. The suite hotel clearly covers the room basics and has fitness/pool, just not the hot tub.
No hot tub is not a dealbreaker for Portland. The rating under 4 is more of an issue. But being able to walk to the lab is tempting with orthotics materials.

That’s the real trade-off: guesthouse wins if the lab gives you secure storage and an easy Friday load-in, because you can avoid commuting with materials. Suite hotel wins if you want the room to be predictable and the mornings to be easier. If campus parking is simple, the suite hotel becomes the cleaner choice.
Would I need a rental car there, or could this be rideshares?

If you choose the guesthouse, skip the rental unless you plan side trips. Airport rideshare plus walking should work. If you choose the suite hotel, rideshares can still work, but only if the host confirms you can drop materials Friday and leave them secured through Sunday. A rental only makes sense if parking and load-in are confirmed; otherwise it adds cost and downtown-campus hassle.
List the questions we need answered before booking.

For the university host: 1) What time can I access the lab Friday, and who unlocks it? 2) Is there a loading zone near the lab entrance for orthotics materials? 3) Can materials be stored securely Friday through Sunday? 4) What time should I plan for Sunday teardown and debrief to end? 5) Is visitor parking available Saturday/Sunday, and does it require a permit? 6) If I use rideshare, which entrance should I use?
Also ask the guesthouse directly about queen bed, in-room coffee, mini-fridge, and fitness access. If they cannot confirm those, the suite hotel probably wins.

Added. Guesthouse questions: confirm bed type, confirm in-room coffee maker, confirm refrigerator or mini-fridge in the room, confirm whether campus rec or any fitness room access is included, and confirm cancellation terms. I’ll also ask whether rooms have air conditioning controls, since late July can be uncomfortable if it’s central-only.
Do not book yet. Track the safe flight and the noonish Monday return, but wait for lab access and hotel answers.

Done. Portland is not booked. Working plan is Friday 8:05 a.m. TPA-PDX arriving 1:42 p.m., Monday 12:15 p.m. PDX-TPA arriving 10:05 p.m., suite hotel as the current reliability lead, guesthouse as the proximity backup only if it confirms the room basics and campus storage/load-in are easy. I’ll wait on host and guesthouse answers before committing.
